races.name: Sodexo Live! 2yo Series EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Hamilton Park 2yo Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Little Lady Karen
runners_data.note: Expensive newcomer with unknown running style but strong Dark Angel/Accidental Agent pedigree suggests class, though Burke's 13/49 recent record raises trainer form concerns.
runners_data.spotlight: 52,000gns foal, £68,000 yearling; first foal; dam twice-raced half-sister to 1m Group 1 winner Accidental Agent, out of 5f 2yo/7f winner (RPR 90); this Dark Angel newcomer takes on rivals who have shown plenty of promise but she's from a top northern stable and could have a big say.

runners_data.name: Meennaa
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who should get easy lead, with 31 days since debut potentially sharpening her but Watson's 2/31 strike rate indicates stable struggles.
runners_data.spotlight: 225,000gns yearling whose dam was a very talented 2yo; backed into 4-1 when clear second on last month's debut at Kempton (6f, AW); there have been mixed messages from that form but it was a promising start to her career and she's travelled from Lambourn for this second start; has to be respected.

runners_data.name: Angels Passing
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who ran creditably in Listed company at York on debut, suggesting she has more ability than this grade and benefits from the likely pace setup.
runners_data.comment: 130,000euros yearling; by No Nay Never; sole debutante in the field; check the betting
runners_data.spotlight: 18-1 and slowly away before keeping on well for fourth of ten on debut in a Listed race at York (5f, good) three weeks ago; this 130,000euros yearling could have plenty more to offer tackling 6f; strong claims.

runners_data.name: Jazz Queen
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type whose Haydock flop followed a promising Chester second, with the 5-pound claiming jockey potentially a negative tactical factor.
runners_data.comment: Chester runner-up; takes on some very interesting newcomers but sets useful form standard
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointing 15-8 shot at Haydock (6f, good to soft) a fortnight ago on her third start; however, prior to that she went close in a maiden at Chester (5.5f, good) and can be in the mix if back on song.

races.paceDynamic: Meennaa will take this race forward from the gates with her prominent style, likely getting an uncontested lead given the lack of other early pace. Little Lady Karen as a debutant brings unknown pace intentions but unlikely to challenge Meennaa early. Both Angels Passing and Jazz Queen are confirmed hold-up performers who will settle towards the rear and rely on late kicks. This sets up perfectly for the hold-up horses who can sit behind a moderate tempo and unleash superior finishing speed in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Meennaa sets steady fractions allowing closers to wind up
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop suits Angels Passing and Jazz Queen who can use their finishing kicks, with Angels Passing having shown better form in stronger company at York. Both hold-up runners benefit from the tactical setup with Meennaa unable to quicken when challenged.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Meennaa Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays very slow and Meennaa retains enough kick
scenarios.body: Her class edge from the 225,000gns purchase price tells, and she uses race fitness advantage over the debuts/returning runners. The prominent position becomes winning if she can resist late challenges on ground that should suit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Little Lady Karen Debuts
scenarios.trigger: If the expensive newcomer shows natural ability and settles kindly
scenarios.body: The Dark Angel filly benefits from her pedigree advantage and Burke's excellent juvenile record, finding a winning run from an unknown position. Her 52,000gns to £68,000 price rise suggests market confidence was justified in the sales ring.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jazz Queen Bounces Back
scenarios.trigger: If Palmer's filly reproduces her Chester second-place form
scenarios.body: She overcomes the Haydock disappointment and uses her proven ability on similar going conditions. The step back up to 6f from 5f helps her settle better for Jack Nicholls.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Little Lady Karen shows early speed rather than settling, as this could pressure Meennaa and change the entire pace complexion.
Monitor Meennaa's jumping from the gates - if she's slow away, the race loses its only confirmed pace angle.
Observe Angels Passing's position after the first furlong to see if she settles kindly or gets further back than ideal.
Check Jazz Queen's early positioning with the inexperienced claimer, as poor placement could negate her finishing ability.
Watch for any market moves on Little Lady Karen that might signal stable confidence in the expensive debutant.

races.name: Morton Fraser Macroberts LLP Handicap

runners_data.name: Novak
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely pace scenario, recent Ayr second shows current form, though 6f drop back from 7f efforts is untested
runners_data.comment: Close fifth of seven over 1m at Ayr recently and he may appreciate the return to 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Went close to ending a losing sequence when runner-up at Ayr (7f, good to firm) recently; slow ground would pose a question and the drop back to 6f isn't an obvious plus, but the stiff finish helps to compensate; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Kelpie Grey
runners_data.note: Prominent style puts him in the danger zone for traffic, dangerous low mark after long losing run, solid recent fifth suggests readiness
runners_data.comment: Return to form needed but he's well handicapped on last year's best efforts here
runners_data.spotlight: His losing sequence goes back 16 races to May 2024 and his form has gone the wrong way; however, he's dropped to a dangerous mark and ran respectably when fifth of nine over 7f at Ayr a fortnight ago (11-8 favourite), when shaping as though the return to 6f may help; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist perfectly placed for this shape, strong 5f form suggests 6f return ideal, two recent seconds show current ability
runners_data.comment: Flashed home after fluffing start at Hamilton (5f) on Friday eve; 1lb lower; key player.
runners_data.spotlight: Two 5f wins last October (good/AW) and runner-up over that trip on last two starts (good/good to firm), finishing well each time and shaping as though this return to 6f is well worth exploring; could play a leading role if conditions suit; best turf efforts have come on good/good to firm.

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong Hamilton record, recent form disappointing but venue specialist angle significant, 17 days since last run
runners_data.comment: All sprint handicap wins on soft or slower; back on last winning mark; wants rain
runners_data.spotlight: Underwhelming on his three starts since promising reappearance run at Doncaster in March; however, he has a strong record at Hamilton and is running here for the first time this season; slow ground would be a positive.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner will ensure honest pace, Hamilton debutant with nine career wins here creates venue angle, mixed 2024 form concern
runners_data.comment: Eleven turf wins include one C&D; weighted to find another race; staying-on 4th latest
runners_data.spotlight: Her form has been mixed this season and she was soundly beaten at Carlisle last time; however, she's running at Hamilton for the first time this year and nine of her 11 wins have come over C&D; she's 10lb lower than when winning here last August and could bounce back with a bold show.

runners_data.name: Carlton And Co
runners_data.note: Lead style but 24-day break since disappointing Catterick run, three wins late last year show ability, may need this run
runners_data.comment: Three wins in the second half of 2025 but it's possible she'll need this comeback run
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field on last month's reappearance at Catterick but may have needed that run; won three times in the second half of last year (6f/7f, good/AW) and is not discounted; has run well on good to soft going.

runners_data.name: Belsito
runners_data.note: Prominent style puts him in traffic danger zone, course and distance winner last September, 36-day break and top weight concern
runners_data.spotlight: Won two in a row over C&D last September (good to soft/soft) and returned to form with very close fourth at Southwell (6f, AW) in April on his second start of the season; slow ground would be a major boost to his claims.

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Prominent runner struggling this season, 2024 form dire despite July Catterick win, market check essential given yard's mixed record
runners_data.comment: Broke duck over 7f at Catterick last July but nothing comparable since, including in 2026
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Catterick (7f, good to firm) last July when 6lb higher; a market check is advised but she's struggled so far this season.

runners_data.name: Wish This
runners_data.note: Prominent style in congested race spells trouble, Newcastle AW win in blinkers his best recent effort, turf form well below that level
runners_data.comment: Recorded sole success in 6f AW event; not the percentage call
runners_data.spotlight: Won in first-time blinkers at Newcastle (6f, AW) last November but he's been well below that level in cheekpieces/blinkers on AW/turf on his three outings this spring.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 58-day break, recent AW wins show current form, turf record includes Curragh soft ground success
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten a neck at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) in March on third stable start then went one better at Southwell (7f, AW); won on turf at the Curragh (6f, soft) last March and this stiff 6f could be a good fit; she's one to consider, especially if slow ground prevails.

races.paceDynamic: Carlton And Co and Iris Dancer will contest the early lead in this 6f handicap, creating an honest gallop from the off. With four horses (Kelpie Grey, Belsito, Invincible Ruby, Wish This) wanting prominent positions, traffic problems are inevitable approaching the final 2f as they converge. The dual pace angle should create a steady tempo rather than burn-out, but the prominent congestion will cause shuffling and interference. This race shape strongly favors the hold-up horses who can avoid the early scrimmaging and benefit from the solid pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack causes interference 2f out as predicted
scenarios.body: The early pace sets it up perfectly for Novak, Thunderstorm Katie and Impressor to pick off the faltering leaders. Hold-up specialists get the clearest runs while prominent runners get hampered.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runners survive
scenarios.trigger: If Carlton And Co or Iris Dancer get an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: Without severe early pressure, one of the pace-setters kicks clear in the final furlong. The prominent pack fails to organize an effective challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent horse emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Belsito or Kelpie Grey avoid the traffic chaos
scenarios.body: A well-positioned prominent runner gets the perfect trip while others suffer interference. Class tells as they surge through late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders go too fast and prominent pack struggles
scenarios.body: The front two burn out completely and the prominent quartet gets tangled up. A horse from further back sweeps up at big odds.

watchPoints.text: Carlton And Co and Iris Dancer early pace battle could be more fierce than expected, burning both out
Prominent quartet of Kelpie Grey, Belsito, Invincible Ruby, Wish This will cause severe traffic problems 2f out
Thunderstorm Katie stepping up from 5f to 6f after two runner-up efforts over shorter trip
Impressor has strong Hamilton record but recent form away from this venue has been poor
Belsito carrying top weight of 135lbs after 36-day absence, fitness question despite class advantage

races.name: Weatherbys Global Stallions Handicap

runners_data.name: Obito
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who needed his reappearance run 20 days ago and has strong course form with two wins here
runners_data.spotlight: Always towards the rear on reappearance over C&D (good) three weeks ago but may have needed that run; won twice last summer (1m/1m2f, good; including here) and he's on a competitive mark on last autumn's form (including on soft ground); he can be in the mix if bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: Proven at this level but drops significantly in class from recent Doncaster Listed success
runners_data.comment: Positive signs when third over 1m here (stable debut) recently; is dangerously handicapped
runners_data.spotlight: Awarded the Spring Mile at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) last March and he's fully 12lb lower today; ran well in defeat at Ayr last month on first two starts for this yard (1m/1m1f, good to firm) and he's on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Qitaal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who was denied clear run when second at Leicester and shows solid recent form
runners_data.comment: Three turf wins at up to 1m2f, the latest in 2024; not gone on from good AW comeback run
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent and without a win since September 2024; however, he was denied a clear run when second of six at Leicester (1m2f, good to firm) recently and can be in the shake-up if backing that up; versatile ground-wise.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Has been mixing codes recently and prominent style could suit if returning to flat form
runners_data.comment: 0-8 over hurdles but went very close at Carlisle in March; can't be ignored
runners_data.spotlight: Twice placed over hurdles this spring (2m1f, good to soft/good), with a heavy defeat on the Flat at Musselburgh (1m6f, soft) in between; however, it's possible this shorter trip will be a better fit for him in this code.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: Front-runner who gets uncontested lead but has been off for 20 days since disappointing at York where he raced wide
runners_data.comment: Big field may not be ideal but he's otherwise in top form and bidding for hat-trick
runners_data.spotlight: Made all twice in a row in April (8.3f/1m, good); down the field at York (7f, good) but that was in a big field and he raced wide; could bounce back with a bold show if conditions suit (well beaten on soft going last November but displayed signs of promise on such ground early in career).

runners_data.name: Zowal
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 58-day break but showed encouraging form before his absence
runners_data.spotlight: Encouraging reappearance run in the Spring Mile at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) and he built on that to win at Pontefract (1m, good to soft); there's every chance that he'll be fine at this longer trip and he's respected.

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister
runners_data.note: Course winner who carries 5lb claimer but has been well beaten in both starts this season
runners_data.comment: Three C&D wins last year and she may be able to leave her reappearance run miles behind
runners_data.spotlight: Won here in 2024 and added three wins at Ayr last year; she's below her last winning mark but has been well beaten on both outings this spring and a major turnaround is necessary.

runners_data.name: Draupnir
runners_data.note: Promising type who was fifth here three weeks ago and prominent running style suits race shape
runners_data.comment: Good third at Thirsk on return; back up in trip with hood on now and he rates a player
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Thirsk (7f, soft) last September and reappeared with promising third there (7f, good) in April; kept on for fifth over this C&D (good) three weeks ago in a race that favoured those ridden more prominently, and the first-time hood may not have suited (left off today); possible player.

runners_data.name: Tee Aitch Aye
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner when conditions were softer but has been tailed off recently
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D (soft) last September when 1lb higher and he's one to watch in the betting, especially if the ground is on the slow side; however, he's been tailed off on both starts this season.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Olly will take the field along from the start as the sole confirmed front-runner, likely getting an uncontested lead through moderate fractions. The prominent runners Qitaal, Mr Lincoln and Draupnir will track him but won't apply serious early pressure, allowing Highland Olly to dictate terms. With most of the field sitting back (Obito, Pearl Eye, Zowal, Penelope's Sister, Tee Aitch Aye all hold-up types), this creates a classic scenario where the pace-setter gets soft sectionals before the hold-up brigade launch their challenges in the final 2-3 furlongs. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will unfold behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Highland Olly Sustains Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Highland Olly gets easy fractions and sees out the trip strongly
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader builds a decisive advantage through moderate pace, then has enough left to repel late challenges. Hold-up horses get caught in traffic or leave their runs too late on ground that's riding faster than advertised.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Traffic Dodge
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses gets a clean run through and benefits from the steady pace
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace sets up perfectly for a closer who avoids the inevitable bottleneck, with Obito or Pearl Eye finding daylight when others are shuffling. Highland Olly's lack of recent competition tells late on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Qitaal or Draupnir position perfectly to strike turning for home
scenarios.body: The prominent horses get the best of both worlds - avoiding early pace pressure but also steering clear of traffic problems further back. They can time their challenge perfectly as Highland Olly begins to tire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Favours Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a muddling affair with multiple hard-luck stories
scenarios.body: The steady pace and crowded finish creates multiple incidents, allowing a horse like Tee Aitch Aye or Penelope's Sister to benefit from others' misfortune. The form book gets turned upside down through circumstances.

watchPoints.text: Highland Olly breaking from the stalls sharply as he needs to establish position immediately to control the race
Obito and Pearl Eye settling positions in the first furlong as both need clean passages from hold-up spots
The pace through the first half-mile as Highland Olly could go too slow and set up a sprint finish
Qitaal's position turning for home as he was denied a clear run last time and needs racing room
Zowal's fitness levels after 58 days off as he showed good form before his break

races.name: Weatherbys Digital Solutions Clyde Handicap

runners_data.name: Diego Ventura
runners_data.note: Prominent racer dropping significantly in grade from Group/Listed company but 21 days since last run may leave him short of peak fitness for this stamina test.
runners_data.spotlight: He's tended to ply his trade in Group and Listed races and he was a Listed winner at Longchamp (7f, good to soft) last May; beaten just under 4l when seventh of 18 at York (1m, good) three weeks ago on his first handicap start and this is less competitive; could be in the mix.

runners_data.name: Al Mubhir
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer perfectly suited by strong pace but 33-day break and poor recent Australian form raises serious fitness concerns.
runners_data.spotlight: Listed win at Sandown in July 2024 and well treated on that form; however, he drew a blank during his 2025 Australian campaign and was soundly beaten on last month's stable debut in the Thirsk Hunt Cup; something to prove.

runners_data.name: Botanical
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits if pace collapses but failed to settle at Newmarket last time and Jack Nicholls' 5lb claim valuable for in-form Burke stable.
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at Newmarket last month but he failed to settle and looked unsuited by the track; prior to that he was a promising fourth in the Lincoln at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) on his stable debut and there's mileage in his mark on his old form; has won over C&D and he's one to consider.

runners_data.name: Theoryofeverything
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist whose four wins came on soft ground, so good to firm surface presents genuine going concern despite recent York fifth.
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well when fifth of 18 at York (1m, good) three weeks ago on his second start of the season; his four wins (one here) have come on soft going so slower ground today would aid his cause; could be a contender.

runners_data.name: Altareq
runners_data.note: Front-runner with promising third on stable debut for Goldie, should ensure honest gallop but significant step up in trip from recent 1m2f efforts.
runners_data.spotlight: Went close in Newbury maiden (1m2f, good) last May on third and final outing for Gosdens and, having been detached early, he was a very promising third of 15 on his stable/handicap debut at York (1m2f, good) three weeks ago; well bred and could take a sizeable step forward from that latest effort.

runners_data.name: Eternal Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 68-day break after Lincoln seventh, improved gelded form last year but fitness must be questioned.
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 3-3 since being gelded (good to firm/good to soft) when winning by 3l at Haydock (1m) last October; reappeared with respectable seventh of 21 in the Lincoln at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) and this lightly raced 4yo could build on that latest effort today; firmly in calculations.

runners_data.name: Two B Tanned
runners_data.note: Front-running specialist with excellent course record, won five times last season making all but 28 days since Musselburgh victory may blunt her speed.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up on 1m Musselburgh reappearance and 9lb well in compared to future mark
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who won five times last April-July (1m-1m1f) and improved again when making all at Musselburgh (1m, good) in April on her reappearance; well beaten at Redcar 11 days later when unpenalised and 8lb higher mark has now kicked in, but she's not written off; unproven on slow ground.

races.paceDynamic: Two B Tanned and Altareq will ensure a genuine gallop from the start, with both confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead over this stamina-testing 1m4f trip. Their honest pace will stretch the field and create a true test of stamina, particularly as both have recent winning form when allowed to dictate. The sustained gallop will expose any lack of fitness or stamina weakness in the field. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven stamina who can finish strongly off a solid pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders maintain a genuine gallop throughout and the pace doesn't collapse
scenarios.body: The strong early pace will set up perfectly for Al Mubhir, Theoryofeverything and Eternal Force to unleash late runs. The stamina test will find out the prominent racers who may struggle to sustain their effort.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Two B Tanned and Altareq go too fast early and both weaken significantly
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactical with no sustained pace, allowing prominent racers Diego Ventura and Botanical to capitalise with superior class. Late runners may find insufficient pace to aim at and struggle to make ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Survive
scenarios.trigger: If Two B Tanned maintains her front-running form from Musselburgh win and gets tactical fractions
scenarios.body: The mare's recent winning form when making all suggests she could dictate at her own pace and prove tough to peg back. Altareq could also benefit if allowed to settle just off the pace rather than being forced into a speed duel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Exposes All
scenarios.trigger: If the combination of trip, pace and good to firm ground proves too demanding for the entire field
scenarios.body: The race becomes a war of attrition where fitness and recent form becomes crucial, potentially suiting the most race-fit runners. Class horses returning from breaks or those stepping up significantly in trip may struggle to deliver their best.

watchPoints.text: Two B Tanned and Altareq engaging in early speed duel could compromise both front-runners and set up back-markers perfectly.
Theoryofeverything's going preference for soft conditions makes him vulnerable on this good to firm surface despite recent York encouragement.
Eternal Force's 68-day absence following Lincoln run needs monitoring for any signs of rustiness in betting or paddock inspection.
Al Mubhir's Australian campaign produced no form of note and 33-day gap since return suggests he may need this run badly.
Botanical's tendency to race freely could prove costly if he fails to settle again like at Newmarket last month.

races.name: Aspire Cleaning & Facilities Ltd Handicap

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning to 5f where he's most effective, though 36 days off and questionable recent form are concerns.
runners_data.comment: Below par since scoring at Wolverhampton (6f, Class 5; 6-4 fav) in March; risks attached.
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Wolverhampton (6f, Class 5; 6-4 favourite) in March but below that level in three subsequent starts, 2l fifth of eight at Musselburgh (5f; 15-2) latest; vulnerable on those performances.

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner whose 216-day break is a major worry despite his consistent record when fresh in previous seasons.
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple winner who lacks a recent run but he's consistent in the main and not handicapped out of it; market could be informative.

runners_data.name: Call To Action
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good current form who disappointed last time but returns to his preferred 5f distance.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 5yo; fine second at Pontefract on return; still of interest despite 2lb rise
runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 with a win and better than ever when a close second of eight at Pontefract (5f, good) on reappearance; Thirsk was disappointing but that was a Class 4, so this is easier.

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Removing headgear after his course and distance win suggests confidence, though his consistency remains questionable.
runners_data.comment: Narrow winner at Hamilton (5f, Class 6, good; from 4lb lower) latest; this demands more.
runners_data.spotlight: Headgear removed and doubled his tally with a narrow win over C&D (good; 3lb lower) a month ago; consistency hasn't always been his forte but clearly a possible contender.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Classic closer who won his last start in similar conditions and will benefit from any pace pressure up front.
runners_data.spotlight: Hit and miss but it was career win number nine when narrowly scoring at Carlisle 17 days ago (5f, good), coming from off the pace; 4lb higher here.

runners_data.name: Lion's House
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose turf form is poor compared to his all-weather exploits, making him hard to fancy here.
runners_data.spotlight: Has only won on Tapeta and spends a lot of his time at Newcastle; finished well behind in his last two races on turf.

races.paceDynamic: Parisiac will likely take up the running with Call To Action and Hi Lord tracking close behind in the early stages. The pace should be genuine but not overly strong given the 5f trip and relatively small field. Water Of Leith, Harb, and Lion's House will settle towards the rear looking to mount late challenges. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish fast, as the front-runners will have enough pace on to set things up for closers over this sharp 5f at Hamilton.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuine but not excessive, allowing closers optimal conditions
scenarios.body: The front three will soften each other up sufficiently for the back-markers to sweep past in the final furlong. Harb and Water Of Leith particularly benefit from their preferred tactical position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Parisiac breaks cleanly and the pace becomes moderate with limited early pressure
scenarios.body: The long absence won't matter as Parisiac controls the race from the front and kicks clear. Call To Action may track him through but lacks the finishing speed to catch him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses fail to get competitive runs or the pace collapses completely
scenarios.body: Call To Action and Hi Lord will have ideal positions to strike and their recent form gives them the edge. The race becomes a battle between the prominent pair in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Parisiac goes too slow early and everyone gets into contention turning for home
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint finish where any horse can win depending on traffic and luck. Lion's House could benefit from the lack of pace despite his poor turf record.

watchPoints.text: Parisiac's market position will reveal connections' confidence after his 216-day absence.
Water Of Leith needs a strong early pace to set up his finishing kick but may lack race fitness.
Call To Action must bounce back from his Thirsk disappointment to justify his prominent market position.
Harb's ability to get a clear run from his hold-up position will be crucial given the small field size.
Hi Lord's headgear removal suggests trainer confidence but watch for any early keen tendencies.

races.name: Sodexo Live! Events Handicap

runners_data.name: Sure And Stedfast
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who returned to form with third here last month and should benefit from the expected strong pace
runners_data.comment: Not that consistent but won twice last summer; no show at 33-1 for recent return in a hood
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form when third here (1m3f, good) last month on second run of the season; also effective on soft ground; could play a leading role if seeing out this longer trip, and there can be optimism on that score.

runners_data.name: Jujubella
runners_data.note: Hold-up type struggling for form this season but handicapper has dropped her 4lbs since last win
runners_data.comment: Respectable efforts in Class 2 contests at York & Doncaster last autumn; more modest since
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten last month on her two runs this year (1m2f/1m1f) and arrives with something to prove, but she's 4lb lower than when winning at Haydock (11.6f, good) last July and the step up in trip may be a positive; stable has won the last two runnings of this race with Two Auld Pals; not written off.

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: Another hold-up horse returning from 107-day break but proven course winner who could improve for the run
runners_data.comment: Best to forgive latest effort; 7lb below last winning mark; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time turf winner who went close at Wolverhampton (1m6f, AW) in February when last seen; not discounted but it's possible this 8yo will improve for this first run since; question mark about slow ground nowadays.

runners_data.name: Glasses Up
runners_data.note: 11yo front-runner who may struggle to lead against younger pace rivals despite decent recent third at Ayr
runners_data.comment: Veteran who ran well for third at his beloved Ayr 16 days ago; chance with a repeat
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo who was a close third over 1m1f at Ayr two starts ago and is versatile trip-wise; however, Ayr brings out the best in him and he was well beaten at Musselburgh last time; 0-4 here, with last visit coming last June.

runners_data.name: Clansman
runners_data.note: Front-runner with two recent wins but all turf victories came on soft ground, not today's good conditions
runners_data.spotlight: Two AW wins from the front this spring (1m4f/2m), the latest at Southwell in April when last seen; he's a six-time winner on turf, with all those coming on soft/heavy going; claims enhanced if slow ground prevails.

runners_data.name: Kisiyra
runners_data.note: Prominent runner having first start for 363 days which is a major concern despite showing ability last June
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish 5yo who is 0-8; not beaten far when fourth of six at 66-1 at Thirsk (1m4f, good) last June on her stable debut and sole outing of the season, but she's back from another absence today and it may be best to look elsewhere; wears a first-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Perseus Way
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from hurdles win but showed C&D ability when winning here last September
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D (good to soft) last September and he's just 1lb higher today; won over hurdles at Hexham (2m4f, soft) last month on his second start for this yard and there's lots to like about his claims.

runners_data.name: Gallus Norman
runners_data.note: Front-runner in excellent form with recent Musselburgh wins and handles good ground well
runners_data.comment: Good step forward when second on handicap debut here last month (1m4f); more to come at 2m
runners_data.spotlight: Improved form when runner-up on handicap debut at Musselburgh (1m4f, good) in April and easily made all back there (2m, good) a fortnight ago; he enjoyed the run of the race last time but a 6lb rise isn't harsh in view of this unexposed 7yo's dominance; has to be respected.

races.paceDynamic: Clansman, Gallus Norman, and Glasses Up will ensure a genuine gallop from the outset, with all three having strong front-running tendencies and recent form suggesting they'll press forward aggressively. The pace will be testing throughout this 1m5f trip, particularly with Clansman coming off front-running wins and Gallus Norman fresh from making all at Musselburgh. With three confirmed pace-setters in a small field, the early fractions will be solid but sustainable over this staying distance. This strong gallop will definitively favour hold-up horses who can finish strongly, as the pace-setters will soften each other up for late challengers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners engage in a prolonged duel through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will take its toll on Clansman, Gallus Norman and Glasses Up, creating perfect conditions for the hold-up horses to strike late. Sure And Stedfast and Perseus Way are best positioned to capitalize with their proven finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Clansman or Gallus Norman can steal a march and dictate moderate fractions
scenarios.body: Without sufficient early pressure, one of the pace-setters can control the race and prove too strong in the finish. Gallus Norman's recent front-running success gives him the edge in this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Kisiyra can track the pace and benefit from her lengthy absence
scenarios.body: The 5yo gets the perfect setup behind the battling leaders and her class tells despite the long layoff. Her prominent style allows her to avoid the early pace battle while staying close enough to pounce.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Moderate Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners show mutual respect and go steadily early
scenarios.body: Without genuine pressure, the race becomes a sprint finish where raw speed matters most. This tactical affair would suit horses with turn of foot rather than pure stamina.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Clansman struggles on good ground as all six turf wins came on soft conditions
Monitor Kisiyra for market support as 363-day absence is extreme even with previous ability shown
Observe early pace development between Gallus Norman and Glasses Up as both need to lead
Check Perseus Way's fitness after 258-day turf absence despite recent hurdles success
Watch for late moves from Sure And Stedfast and Annandale as hold-up horses in small field

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Handicap

runners_data.name: Sophiesticate
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning to preferred longer trip after disappointing over inadequate 1m distance
runners_data.comment: Stays further and offered little back over 1m at Newcastle in early December
runners_data.spotlight: Below par on final two starts last year and same story on recent reappearance over 1m at Ayr; however, she's back up to a more suitable trip today and is 6lb below her last winning mark; not written off.

runners_data.name: Dandy's Angel
runners_data.note: Needs further than recent 8.4f efforts, hold-up style suits if pace develops properly
runners_data.spotlight: Beverley specialist who hasn't been at the top of her game over 8.4f there on her two starts this season; however, that trip is probably inadequate nowadays and she has a reduced mark to work with back up in trip; has won over C&D and this 9yo is not written off.

runners_data.name: Ravenswell
runners_data.note: Hold-up type coming off poor 2m effort but better suited to this intermediate distance
runners_data.comment: Should have a small race in him but he returns from 237 days off with stamina to prove
runners_data.spotlight: He will have something to prove if slow ground prevails and he was tailed off on his recent reappearance over 2m at Musselburgh; however, that was his first run beyond 1m3f and he went close over that trip at Carlisle last August, when 2lb higher; might not be a forlorn hope back down in trip.

runners_data.name: Hijo De La Luna
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 71-day break, first-time visor previously effective
runners_data.comment: Won basement-grade AW race in February but overall profile not persuasive
runners_data.spotlight: Won a classified race at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) in February in a first-time visor; however, down the field at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) in March and well beaten back over hurdles in April; needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with solid recent Doncaster form over similar distances
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win from her 17 starts but she's run really well in defeat at Doncaster on both turf outings this season (1m2f/1m4f, good to soft/good) and there's every chance she'll be bang there once more.

runners_data.name: Sugarpiehoneybunch
runners_data.note: Previous course winner who needed recent reappearance after 50-day layoff
runners_data.comment: Won at Hamilton in June after a longer break than this; may go well on this comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten on final three starts last season and same story on reappearance in April; however, she might have needed that latest outing and she won this last year; shouldn't be discounted.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Prominent early but disappointing recent form suggests he's below best level
runners_data.comment: Won off this mark on AW last August but soundly beaten on his three outings this spring
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) last August and runner-up at Musselburgh (1m4f, good to soft) next time; however, he's been well below that level so far this season and a major turnaround is necessary.

runners_data.name: Ivynator
runners_data.note: Returning after 307-day absence with poor recent record, needs everything to fall right
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up over hurdles last May but this 8yo has struggled to get competitive on his four starts since, one of those being on the Flat; races for the first time since last September and others make greater appeal.

runners_data.name: Wath Court
runners_data.note: Longstanding maiden with pattern of fading in finish, needs miracle improvement
runners_data.comment: Maiden; soundly beaten in handicaps for this trainer in 2026, including at this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Longstanding maiden who has been well beaten on all four starts this year and would be a surprise winner today.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Limited experience hold-up type who fades late and lacks competitive form
runners_data.comment: 4yo who has raced only five times but well beaten last autumn in her first two handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo who has raced only six times but has been well beaten in her three handicaps, the latest her reappearance at Musselburgh in April.

runners_data.name: Uncle Liam
runners_data.note: Only natural front-runner with stamina doubts but huge tactical advantage
runners_data.comment: Encouraging Ayr eighth on return, leading until 1f out; merits serious consideration
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden who arrives with plenty to prove regarding current form and stamina (untested at trip); however, his pedigree provides optimism regarding him staying and he could stage a revival when back on slow ground.

races.paceDynamic: Uncle Liam is the only confirmed front-runner and will likely get an uncontested lead with Hijo De La Luna and Falaise Blanc sitting prominent. The majority field comprises hold-up horses (Sophiesticate, Dandy's Angel, Ravenswell, Recobella, Sugarpiehoneybunch, Wath Court, Storm On Jura) who will need the pace to develop. With minimal early pressure, Uncle Liam can dictate fractions and kick clear, while the hold-up brigade may struggle to peg back a moderate tempo over this staying trip. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and the lone pace-setter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncle Liam Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Uncle Liam gets an easy lead and quickens off steady fractions
scenarios.body: The 4yo can use his tactical advantage to build a winning margin before the hold-up horses get organized. His stamina questions become irrelevant if he's not pressed early and can control the gallop throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and develops into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The abundance of hold-up horses creates a cavalry charge scenario where the best finishers can overcome the tactical disadvantage. Recobella and Sophiesticate's recent form suggests they have the class to capitalize.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Hijo De La Luna or Falaise Blanc press Uncle Liam early
scenarios.body: The pace increases enough to set up the race for closers but Uncle Liam's advantage is compromised by being forced to work harder. The prominent pair tire from their efforts leaving the race to late runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Uncle Liam fails to stay or fades dramatically in the straight
scenarios.body: His stamina doubts prove founded and he stops quickly, turning the race into chaos where any hold-up horse with a turn of foot can capitalize. The field bunches up creating a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Uncle Liam's market support - if well-backed suggests connections confident about stamina
Early pace development - if Hijo De La Luna or Falaise Blanc press the leader immediately
Recobella's position turning in - her hold-up style needs room and time to be effective
Ground conditions deteriorating - several runners have going concerns if it turns softer
Jockey tactics on the hold-up horses - whether they commit early or wait for late dash
